faq.a: The reason wasn't disclosed. PopStroke pulled out of its planned mini golf site in early 2026, and the Village Council asked Lotis to return with a new plan for the space.

faq.q: What restaurants are coming to Lotis Wellington?
faq.a: Seasons 52 is under construction and expected in 2027, and Cluck Face Nashville Hot Chicken is preparing to open. Lazy Dog, Frank Pepe and Naked Taco signed on but haven't opened.

title: 620 Apartments Where Nordstrom Used to Be: Smart Fix or the Wrong Move for Wellington?
h1: 620 Apartments Where Nordstrom Used to Be: Smart Fix or the Wrong Move for Wellington?
seoTitle: Wellington Green Nordstrom Apartments: 620-Unit Plan, Pros, Cons & Next Steps
description: A developer wants to replace the empty Nordstrom at The Mall at Wellington Green with 620 apartments. The plan, the traffic study, what supporters and critics say, and what happens next.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic exterior of a large vacant two-story department store at a suburban South Florida mall on a sunny day, empty parking lot, palm trees, modern apartment buildings visible in the distance, no people, no text, no logos, no store signage

faq.q: What is replacing Nordstrom at The Mall at Wellington Green?
faq.a: Bainbridge Companies has proposed demolishing the former Nordstrom and building 620 apartments in three buildings with a clubhouse and parking garage. The plan has not been approved.

faq.q: Has the Wellington Nordstrom apartment plan been approved?
faq.a: No. It needs a master plan amendment through the Village of Wellington's planning and zoning process and public hearings. No hearing dates have been reported.

faq.q: Will the Nordstrom apartments add traffic?
faq.a: The developer's traffic study projects 1,164 fewer daily trips than the former store, with morning rush-hour trips up 146 and evening trips down 158. Some residents still worry about congestion at Forest Hill Blvd and State Road 7.

faq.q: When did Nordstrom close at Wellington Green?
faq.a: Nordstrom opened at the mall in 2003 and closed in April 2019. The space has been mostly vacant since.

title: The Road Wellington Was Promised: Why Lyons Road Still Dead-Ends
h1: The Road Wellington Was Promised: Why Lyons Road Still Dead-Ends
seoTitle: Lyons Road Extension Wellington: Why It Dead-Ends at Lake Worth Road
description: Why doesn't Lyons Road go through in Wellington? The county's State Road 7 traffic trigger, the Ranchettes debate, and what new development along 441 could change.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic suburban South Florida two-lane road that ends at a dead end with a guardrail and tall grass, a rural horse property with white fencing and oak trees beyond, palm trees, warm afternoon light, no people, no text, no signs, no logos

faq.q: Why doesn't Lyons Road go through in Wellington?
faq.a: Palm Beach County only builds the extension when State Road 7 (US 441) between Lake Worth Road and Stribling Way reaches capacity, about 3,590 vehicles in the busiest hour. The road currently carries just under 2,860, according to WFLX.

faq.q: Where does Lyons Road end in Wellington?
faq.a: Lyons Road ends at Lake Worth Road. Drivers heading north detour via State Road 7 and Stribling Way to reach Forest Hill Boulevard.

faq.q: Who opposes the Lyons Road extension?
faq.a: Some residents of the Ranchettes, a rural area of horse properties the extension would run through, oppose it because of its impact on the area's rural character, horses and wildlife.

faq.q: Will Lyons Road ever be extended?
faq.a: It depends on traffic. If growth along State Road 7 from projects like Lotis and Village Landing pushes the road past the county's capacity trigger, the extension could move forward.

title: K-Park Becomes Village Landing: Did Wellington Make the Right Call?
h1: K-Park Becomes Village Landing: Did Wellington Make the Right Call?
seoTitle: K-Park Wellington Sale: Why the Village Chose Related Ross Over a $54M Bid
description: Wellington sold K-Park for about $47 million to Related Ross and Wingrove Academy's founders, passing on a $54 million offer. The history, the debate over green space and traffic, and what's next.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic aerial view of a large open farm field with rows of vegetables beside a busy suburban South Florida road, a shopping center and palm trees at the edge, construction equipment staged at one corner, golden hour, no people, no text, no logos

faq.q: What is K-Park in Wellington?
faq.a: K-Park is about 70 acres on State Road 7 at Stribling Way that the Village of Wellington bought in 2003 for $8.5 million. It is becoming Village Landing and Wingrove Academy.

faq.q: Who bought K-Park?
faq.a: Related Ross bought about 32 acres for $28.3 million for Village Landing, and the western portion is set aside for Wingrove Academy. The total deal was about $47 million.

faq.q: Did Wellington turn down a higher offer for K-Park?
faq.a: Yes. The Palm Beach Post reported a $54 million offer for all of K-Park from the Ward family's W & W VIII LLC. The Village chose Related Ross, citing in part its experience, and counted the school as a plus.

faq.q: When will Village Landing open?
faq.a: Construction is expected to begin in fall 2026, with an opening targeted for 2028.
